v.rationale: I ran `php artisan test` on both: impl-1 passes 17/17 and impl-2 passes 24/24. The two implementations are very close. Their schema, validation rules, scopes, money formatting and query plans are nearly identical (5 queries each). In my probes they returned byte-for-byte equivalent results for: empty params, array status, invalid month, alphanumeric country, a filtered same-day range with a multi-line order, and an order with no items. Neither has a real correctness bug. The only shared quirk is that empty optional params like `?from=` return 422 instead of being ignored. That makes the ranking a matter of idiom and readability. impl-2 splits the report into named methods, uses `orderByDesc`, `select()` and `whereHas` subqueries, and has better tests: a data provider for the 422 cases, plus rounding and formatting checks. impl-1 has one design edge: its FormRequest exposes typed accessors that turn the input into CarbonImmutable values and the enum, whereas impl-2 passes an untyped array and re-parses dates in the report and the scope. But impl-1 puts every sub-report in one large return array, uses `orderByRaw` and concatenated selectRaw column lists, packs all invalid inputs into a single test, and calls factory states by dynamic string in its test helper. On balance impl-2 comes out narrowly ahead.
